# Cerebrum

> Wolfpack/OpenWolf project learning memory.
> Last updated: 2026-07-12

## User Preferences

- Present this enhanced workflow as **Wolfpack**, not vanilla OpenWolf; keep `.wolf/`, `openwolf`, and `openwolf.*` as compatibility/runtime namespaces unless intentionally migrated.
- Do not initialize or use OpenWolf inside AI plugin staging/runtime directories; keep plugin stages minimal and isolated to avoid nested hooks, token waste, daemon confusion, and contaminated model comparisons.
- [2026-08-08] Prefer durable memory that remains plain-file, local, inspectable, and Git-trackable. Avoid making databases or MCP services foundational to Wolfpack memory because the added runtime/state boundary feels fragile; evaluate external memory projects for transferable mechanisms, not infrastructure adoption.
- [2026-08-08] Keep the evidence gate against low-value additions: sample popular AI workflow/memory projects for isolated useful ideas, but adopt only mechanisms that demonstrate better value than their complexity and operational cost. A popular project may contribute one transferable idea—or none—and should not be imported wholesale.
- User runs `openwolf init` before every session; if that command copies from this local fork, future initialized projects receive the fork's current template/runtime behavior.
- [2026-08-09] Wolfpack's recent skill-first addition intentionally encourages selecting an appropriate installed skill before recreating a workflow. The user welcomes those skills launching bounded workflow-backed reviews automatically; distinguish Wolfpack's skill-first policy from the native/installed skill and Workflow implementations it invokes.
- User wants Wolfpack to improve AI git/version discipline: nudge agents to inspect/report git state, avoid broad staging, distinguish pre-existing changes, and consider version/changelog/document revision impacts.
- [2026-07-27] **Commit locally only.** This repo is the user's own fork, well diverged from anything upstream — it has NO git remotes and no `main` branch (default is `master`). Do not offer to push, set an upstream, or open a PR, and do not report "push/PR outstanding" as a pending item. Commit to the working branch and stop there. (The Claude Code environment banner says "Main branch: main", which is wrong here — verify with `git branch -a` before any branch operation.)

## Key Learnings

- [2026-08-19] A peer verdict is input, not authority. Output from a subagent, companion, or panel is evidence to weigh — never a decision to adopt unexamined. This holds in both directions: a CONFIRMED finding still needs its reproduction re-run locally before it drives an edit, and a dismissal still needs its reasoning checked before the finding is dropped. Demonstrated twice in one session: a companion correctly refuted a registry claim I had made (they were right, bug-691), and a challenge sub-agent's round-1 dismissal was itself wrong (bug-702) — accepting either verdict on authority would have produced the wrong outcome. Re-run the claim; the cost is small next to shipping on someone else's error.
- [2026-08-19] Write cerebrum entries to generalize past the incident that produced them. An entry that only recounts one bug is a buglog entry in the wrong file; the durable form names the class, the tell that identifies it next time, and the response — then cites the incident as evidence. Prefer positive phrasing ("assert the denominator", "measure exit status directly") over prohibitions, because a rule stated as a "don't" leaves the correct action unspecified. Keep the evidence link so the specific case is still recoverable.
- [2026-08-19] A hook that blocks should hand back a usable correction, not a refusal. The block message is the model's next-turn context, so a bare "not allowed" wastes the turn and invites a retry of the same shape; naming the safer alternative ("use X instead", "run Y first") converts the block into forward progress. Applies to any gate whose output the model reads — nudges, denials, and validation failures alike.
- [2026-08-08] External memory-system evaluation: the most transferable design is Compozy's plain-file separation of concerns — one stable-ID lesson per Markdown file with Context/Root cause/Rule/Operationalization/Anti-pattern/Evidence, a compact index, and a separate standing-directives file. Engram contributes stable topic keys/upsert semantics, progressive disclosure, lifecycle review, and duplicate metadata; MemPalace contributes strict separation of verbatim evidence from derived disposable indexes plus authored-time provenance; Memori contributes a small closed taxonomy and explicit entity/process/session attribution. ECC adds an important trust boundary: agent-written memory is unreviewed context, not executable instruction; governed rules remain separate, promotion is explicit, malformed memories are excluded without rewrite, and supersession preserves history. Copy these mechanisms into Wolfpack without adopting their DB, MCP, cloud, embedding, daemon, or background-LLM foundations.
- [2026-08-08] Arbor evaluation: its strongest transferable contribution is not another memory system but an evidence-linked hypothesis lifecycle: claim/direction → isolated branch or worktree → actual validation → result → concise lesson, with failed strategies retained and descendants inheriting relevant ancestor evidence. Also valuable are protected-asset SHA-256 manifests that invalidate evidence after evaluator/test tampering, resumable versioned atomic plain-file checkpoints, and explicit strategy-exhaustion stopping. Wolfpack already has worktree tooling, QA reductions, review lineages, and durable dispositions, so adopt these as incremental metadata/policy only when optimizing or comparing competing approaches—not as a new coordinator runtime, MCP server, dashboard, event bus, provider stack, or general task requirement.
- [2026-08-08] DeerFlow 2.0 evaluation: its notable reliability mechanisms—deterministic delegation ledger, repeated-tool loop breaker, current-hash read-before-write gate, token-budget stop reasons, dangling tool-call repair, and typed oversized-output synopsis—are strong implementations for its LangGraph super-agent runtime, but Claude Code/Wolfpack already receives equivalent behavior from native task/agent state, file-tool read guards, harness-persisted output previews, workflow budgets, provider message handling, and Wolfpack convergence controls. Do not recreate runtime middleware merely because its implementation is sophisticated; require an observed gap in Wolfpack first.
- [2026-08-08] Headroom evaluation: raw token reduction is not a sufficient context-optimization metric for cached coding sessions. Mutating a small historical block can cost far more by invalidating a large warm suffix, while edits confined to the uncached live zone remain favorable. Any future Wolfpack context canary must preserve frozen cached prefixes, measure cache-read/write economics on identical real transcripts, and bind savings to unchanged task outcomes. Headroom's provider walkers, lossy compressors, tag protection, reversible store, proxy, MCP, and model stack are not justified without an observed Wolfpack gap. Evidence: `.wolf/qa/headroom-evaluation-2026-08-08.md`.
- [2026-08-08] OpenSpec evaluation: do not add its parallel CLI, generated command set, persistent proposal/spec/design/tasks archive, stores, or customizable artifact-DAG runtime to Wolfpack. Claude Code plan mode plus Wolfpack tasks, QA reductions, current-byte reviews, Experiment Mode, and Git already cover the lifecycle with stronger evidence boundaries than file-existence completion or keyword-based verification. One isolated canary candidate remains: on consequential behavior-changing plans, explicitly map observable acceptance scenarios to planned tasks so missing edge cases and unrequested tasks are structurally visible. Require measured scope-drift/defect reduction before adoption, and exempt trivial fixes/refactors. Evidence: `.wolf/qa/openspec-evaluation-2026-08-08.md`.
- [2026-08-08] `shanraisshan/claude-code-best-practice` evaluation: treat it as an on-demand, fast-moving Claude Code feature index and demonstration catalog, not a framework or instruction source to copy into Wolfpack. Its strongest principles—deterministic hooks, isolated agents, conditional context, skills, model routing, and evidence over anecdotal quality perceptions—already match Wolfpack and native Claude Code. Do not enable more settings, hooks, agents, commands, daily model canaries, or orchestration layers without a concrete observed gap. Verify consequential feature claims against current official docs/CLI because catalogs age quickly. Evidence: `.wolf/qa/claude-code-best-practice-evaluation-2026-08-08.md`.
- [2026-08-08] Hermes Agent evaluation: do not adopt its parallel agent runtime, SQLite/FTS memory, gateway, scheduler, provider/terminal abstraction, context engine, or autonomous curator. Its useful contribution is safety corroboration: automation should inspect current bytes, touch only clearly agent-authored artifacts, archive rather than delete, honor pinned/user-approved material, sanitize untrusted sources (including bidi/zero-width controls), avoid environment-derived identity, and describe file denylists honestly as defense-in-depth when shell access can bypass them. These principles are already covered more strongly by Wolfpack's governed Cerebrum promotion, QA/Experiment evidence, plain-file state, and Claude Code isolation; add no subsystem without a measured gap. Evidence: `.wolf/qa/hermes-agent-evaluation-2026-08-08.md`.
- [2026-08-08] Mem0 evaluation: reject its SDK/plugin/cloud/MCP/vector/graph/SQLite memory platform, per-prompt remote prefetch, frequency-based transcript capture, and equal authority for assistant-generated facts. The isolated ADD-only extractor survived **offline fixture conformance only**: 18/18 protected positives, 0/30 negative acceptances, 9 current-classifier misses recovered, and 0 baseline regressions. This warrants a separate opt-in runtime design review, not integration: proposals remain `trust: "unreviewed"`, Cerebrum promotion stays explicit, and no database/vector/MCP/cloud dependency is justified. The control accepted 5 protected negatives, so future runtime design must evaluate precision as well as recall. Evidence: `.wolf/qa/mem0-evaluation-2026-08-08.md`, `.wolf/qa/mem0-canary-2026-08-08.md`.
- **Project:** customopenwolf.
- `/home/tony/projects/customopenwolf` and `/mnt/j/projectshome/projects/customopenwolf` are the same physical J: drvfs repo; treat them as one git history.
- The fork has a source/runtime/template split: `src/` and source templates drive durable changes, `.wolf/` is the installed runtime payload, and scaffold templates must remain generic.
- Skill integration boundary (2026-08-06): Wolfpack owns obligation detection, state, current-byte verification, and closure; explicit skills perform bounded work and emit compact receipts. A skill receipt never self-certifies. Canonical input identity remains SHA-256 over sorted normalized `[path, hash]` tuples, while provider-specific evidence hashes stay opaque and separate.
- Scientific Mode became default-enabled Claim Calibration: a compact Stop-hook reasoning gate using observation/inference/limit/falsifier framing, with legacy `openwolf.scientific_mode` compatibility during migration.
- Runtime/template changes usually need three-layer sync: source, installed `.wolf/`, and templates/update payloads. Hook behavior often spans `src/hooks/*`, `.wolf/hooks/*`, `templates/wolf/hooks/*`, shared utilities, and config copies.
- Existing-project `openwolf update` must copy helper scripts and sibling `.wolf/utils/*.js` dependencies, not only hook entrypoints.
- Wolfpack-managed Claude skills use an explicit file manifest and overlay only exact owned paths; init/update/backup/restore must never recursively replace `.claude/skills`, because unrelated skills and adjacent files are user-owned.
- [2026-08-06] SkillsBench standard skills are a user-scope generated Claude plugin, not project-managed `.claude/skills`: config/lock/releases live in `~/.openwolf/skillsbench`, upstream uses `~/projects/skillsbench/upstream`, and only the manager-owned marketplace symlink may be replaced.
- [2026-08-06] K-Dense scientific-agent-skills use a second independent user-scope plugin (`scientific-skills@kdense-scientific`) with separate state, checkout, releases, rollback, and schedule; never merge them into SkillsBench or copy them into project `.claude/skills`.
- Fresh init and update must both write `.wolf/utils/package.json` with `type: module`; hook package scope alone does not control sibling utility JavaScript in receiving projects without a root ESM declaration.
- Review gate lifecycle: pending review entries must be completed with `complete-review.js` or `wolfpack review complete`, never by manual JSON edits, so content hashes and reviewer provenance are verified.
- Reviewer recommendations are profile-driven and project-local: `gov/us-only` suppresses non-US/open-profile models; `open` can advertise broader plugins; `budget` should prefer plentiful-token GLM/Kimi/MiMo/MiniMax before escalating.
- Wolfpack review prompts select policy and explicit current files; standardized provider companions own `review --file` staging, subprocesses, redaction, hashing, cleanup, and transport. Companion receipt hashes are not Wolfpack manifest hashes, so stale reviews require refresh, actual current-byte re-review, then `--reviewed-current`.
- Operational evidence defaults to the provider-neutral `/ops:live-debug` and `/ops:deploy-verify` skills. Health and functional probes remain independent, and Wolfpack must not duplicate their collectors.
- Open-profile redteam diversity should include GLM, MiMo, MiniMax when available; GLM-5.2 is a high-value finder/grader candidate, Kimi is useful as an independent contrast grader, and MiMo/MiniMax are good cheap diverse finders.
- DeepSeek and Qwen reviewer plugins are available as non-US open-profile options, but budget guidance should not prefer them because their tokens are not as plentiful.
- Version durable OpenWolf changes by incrementing the custom prerelease suffix and keeping `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, and `VERSION` synchronized.
- Git/version discipline is now a Stop-hook gate: command-level safety nudges (broad staging, destructive Git, commit without cached diff) are always eligible, while status/version footers are materiality-gated to avoid nagging on mini edits.
- PM2 daemon liveness requires `status: "online"` plus a positive integer `pid`; stopped or pid-less PM2 rows are stale and should not count as active daemons.
- Daemon startup/heartbeat paths must refuse missing project/runtime directories and avoid recreating manually deleted project roots by writing `.wolf` state during shutdown.
- Redteam plugin files live outside this repo at `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/tony-local/plugins/redteam/`; QA reductions for external edits made from this repo still belong in this project's `.wolf/qa`.
- Wolfpack's coding-quality controls are hook-based and do not require PM2; the dashboard, cron scheduler, heartbeat, and live broadcasts are optional background services.
- Claude Code client queue lifecycle in transcripts: `queue-operation` `remove` (with content) = taken from queue for mid-turn injection; `dequeue` (no content) = consumed for next-turn delivery; delivery of a mid-turn message is a `{type:"attachment", attachment:{type:"queued_command", prompt}}` entry surfaced as "The user sent a new message while you were working". ~95% of removes in a busy session are harness-internal `<task-notification>` traffic. Watchdog config: `openwolf.queue_drop_watch` (shared.ts `getQueueDropWatchConfig`); tests in tests/queue-watch.test.js.
- `.wolf/.gitignore` (nested) is seeded and overwritten by init/update (ALWAYS_OVERWRITE in both init.ts and update.ts) so runtime churn is ignored in every project without touching the project's root .gitignore. `buglog.json` is deliberately NOT ignored — it is durable knowledge and should be trackable (feedback 2026-07-21). When changing gitignore policy, update the `git check-ignore` assertions in scripts/verify-install.js to match.
- `complete-review.js --check` is the read-only drift probe: exit 0 = CURRENT, 4 = STALE, no reviewlog mutation, no --reviewer required. Use it before deciding whether a pending review needs `--refresh` + re-review.
- The simplicity nudge names the most-edited non-scratch file (≥5 edits, or ≥3 edits + ≥8KB) as a concrete bloat-check target; scratch definition reuses `quality_gate.buglog_scan_excludes`.
- Companion transports fail as a FLEET, not individually: most companions route through shared infrastructure (CLIProxyAPI bridges, `claude -p` runtime), so identical errors across providers (e.g. [1211 Unknown Model], 401) mean one shared outage — 2 failed providers is enough evidence to stop retrying (bug-450). The companion roster for outage fallback: GLM (z.ai direct) and Kimi (own endpoint) have independent transports from the CLIProxyAPI-backed set (chatgpt/codex-spark/mimo).
- Claude Code (2.1.217) renders ANY Stop hook that returns `{"decision":"block","reason":X}` as `Stop hook error: X` in the terminal — "error" is the label for a blocking stop, not a hook failure. Genuine failures render as `Stop hook error occurred` / `Error executing ...`. Wolfpack's static `reason: "Wolfpack feedback"` (stop.ts `exitWithStopHookResult`) therefore always produces a scary-looking but benign line; the real content is the `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` rendered as `Stop hook feedback:`. stop.js only ever writes JSON to stdout + exit 0, and the project hook wrapper `import(...).catch(()=>{})` swallows even crashes silently.

- Nudge convergence architecture (2026-07-26): Stop-hook nudges route through `src/hooks/nudges/` — `state.ts` (fingerprints, dispositions, leases), `engine.ts` (suppress → rank → budget → claim → emit), `project-scope.ts` (ownership), `rules/{cerebrum,conclusion,review}.ts`. The invariant is *the same evidence must not nudge twice unless the evidence materially changes*. Dispositions bind to a SHA-256 of full decision evidence, never to a rule id and never to rendered text. CLI: `wolfpack nudge list|show|resolve|dismiss|snooze|stats`.
- Legacy nudges (git-discipline, review, quality, buglog, simplicity) still format their own prose and bypass the engine's ranking; they are trimmed at the single `emitStopHookFeedback` choke point by `applyLegacyBudget()` in stop.ts. Measured 1865 → 904 chars on a real 3-nudge stop. Migrating a legacy rule = have it return a candidate instead of calling `emitStopHookFeedback`.
- The `.ts`/`.js` twin relationship DIFFERS per directory — never blind-`cp` a `.ts` over its `.js`. `src/utils/size-discipline.js` is **compiled output** (no `@ts-nocheck`, trailing `//# sourceMappingURL=` footer); `.wolf/utils/size-discipline.js` carries an `@ts-nocheck` header; `templates/wolf/` matches `src/`'s `.js`. Under `src/hooks/nudges/rules/`, the `.ts` and `.js` have pre-existing whitespace/comment drift, so edits must be applied surgically per file (exact-anchor edits or perl), then verified with `grep` across all three layers. Confirm any sync with `git show HEAD:<path> | cmp - <path>` so only the intended change remains.
- [2026-08-08] When a hook imports a newly exported TypeScript helper, verify its active source-adjacent JavaScript utility actually exports the same symbol. `src/utils/size-discipline.js` had retained a non-exported `atomicWriteJson` despite the TypeScript export; ESM hooks failed at module instantiation until the compiled/template mirrors exported it.
- Two distinct version constants live in the nudge system and must not be conflated: `NUDGE_STATE_VERSION` (state.ts, currently 2) is the on-disk state-file format; `SCHEMA_VERSION` (each rule, currently 3) participates in the fingerprint hash. Bump the rule `SCHEMA_VERSION` whenever the fingerprint algorithm changes, or stale dispositions keep suppressing nudges that should now fire — verified by hashing identical evidence at v2 vs v3 and confirming the digests differ.
- `.wolf/buglog.json` has real, pre-existing integrity drift: as of 2026-07-26 it holds 188 entries but only 169 unique IDs (16 duplicated IDs, incl. bug-264/265/266 three times each) and 24 entries with no `status` at all, spanning bug-217..bug-470. Any programmatic read MUST assume duplicates — `find(x => x.id === id)` can return the wrong record. See the Do-Not-Repeat entries dated 2026-07-23 and 2026-07-26 for the write-side rules.

- **2026-08-19 — `openwolf update` targeting.** Fleet-wide by default (`update.ts:2`,
  `let selected = allProjects`); `--project <substr>` matches against both name and root.
  Source repo (customopenwolf) self-skips. On the `/mnt/j` WSL2 mount a full fleet update
  takes minutes and sits in uninterruptible disk sleep (state `D`) — that is real I/O, not
  a hang; verify with `/proc/<pid>/status` before killing it.
- **2026-08-19 — Skill `description:` is the routing surface.** Claude matches it against the
  user's request, so provider-specific wording there silently prevents the skill from ever
  firing for equivalent generic phrasing. Skill *bodies* may name providers freely. Linted
  at install in `validateSkill` (bug-705).


## Do-Not-Repeat

- [2026-08-19] A regression test can pin the easy half of a defect class and read as full coverage. `'the dual-resolution fallback still fails on a genuinely absent file'` used `docs/nowhere.md`, which was absent under BOTH candidate paths — so it proved only that a name absent everywhere is caught, a claim a single-base implementation also satisfies. The actual failure mode (one candidate is the real target and absent, the OTHER exists by basename collision) was never constructed, and a real false negative hid behind a green test. When a fix adds an alternative path, the test must make the alternatives DISAGREE, not merely both fail. Evidence: bug-702, `.wolf/qa/challenge-gate.md`.
- [2026-08-19] Challenge a dismissal, not just a confirmation. Running the new Challenge Gate on a finding against my own code: round 1 returned NOT A DEFECT with correct reasoning about the code's *intent* (documented design comment, deliberate trade-off) and was wrong about its *consequence*. Round 2, tasked with arguing the opposite side, produced a working reproduction that reversed the verdict. "Intentional" and "correct" are different claims — a design comment explains why a choice was made, never that it holds. A gate whose second round only re-confirms the first is theatre.
- [2026-08-19] A false-positive storm and a silent pass are the same bug wearing different clothes — both mean the check is not measuring what it claims. `openwolf driftcheck` shipped four resolution defects in one sitting: a `.wolf`-relative base (221 of 222 real files reported missing), pre-heading entries dropped BEFORE the denominator incremented (invisible undercount that `extracted == checked` could not catch, because both stayed consistent), prose headings joined as directories, and entries already carrying their root-relative prefix double-joined. Assert the denominator AND spot-check that a sample of "findings" are genuinely absent on disk; a finding count is not evidence until one is verified by hand. Evidence: bug-695/696/698/699, `.wolf/qa/drift-check-command.md`.
- [2026-08-19] Measure a control's exit status directly, never through a pipe. Three negative controls for the drift check printed `exit=0` while correctly failing, because `cmd | grep ...; echo $?` reports GREP's status, not the command's — the controls appeared to prove the check could not fail. Redirect to a file and test `$?` on the command itself. Evidence: bug-697.
- [2026-08-19] A check that hangs is a check that does not run. `driftcheck` walked every source file to depth 8 for parked-question markers even with no ledger to correlate against — 39s on one project, and 43 of 85 fleet projects timed out entirely. Skip expensive work when its consumer is absent, but make the SKIP text name what went unscanned ("code not scanned for orphan TODO(UQ-n) markers"), never a bare "none found" that implies a scan. Evidence: bug-700, 39s -> 3.7s.
- [2026-08-19] Name the repo a measurement ran against whenever a session spans more than one project. A drift-check demo reported as "against this repo" was run in customopenwolf (extracted=231 missing=10) while reviewing a brief authored from skillsbench (extracted=47 missing=0) — the other session reasonably read it as their file and refuted it as phantom. Both numbers were correct; only the label was ambiguous. Cross-project sessions make bare deictics ("this repo", "here", "the anatomy") unresolvable — print `cwd` with the result, as the reproduction above does.
- [2026-08-18] Directive TOKENS are not directive INTENT. The learning.explicit nudge misfired twice on review-pipeline turns because `never|always|don't` match identically whether the user is issuing guidance or QUOTING it — and handoff/protocol prose is maximally dense in those tokens. Role filtering did not help: a user turn relaying an assistant ship report is still `type:"user"`. Guard on the OPENER (attribution prefix, document-report verb), anchored so a genuine correction that merely mentions a document still fires. Evidence: bug-694, `.wolf/qa/learning-relay-guard.md`.
- [2026-08-18] A staged canary is not ceremony: staging the stage-before-widen rule in ONE project and actually exercising it caught bug-693 (verifier resolved its template from `process.cwd()`, so from any other cwd it silently degraded to heading-only and printed PASS) BEFORE the rule reached 85 projects. Verification tooling itself must be exercised from a foreign cwd — resolve internal assets from `import.meta.url`, never `process.cwd()`, and fail closed when a content binding is unavailable. Evidence: bug-693, control F in `.wolf/qa/fleet-section-coverage-verifier.md`.
- [2026-08-18] Test BOTH halves of an external reviewer's finding on real bytes before accepting or rejecting it. Finding 8 claimed the fleet verifier was vacuous in two ways: heading REMOVAL would pass (measured FALSE — reported `missing=1` and named the project) and body-revert-with-heading-intact would pass (measured TRUE — the superseded rule verified as covered). Accepting the finding wholesale would have "fixed" a working check; rejecting it on the first disproof would have shipped the real content-drift hole. Split-verdict findings are common: confirm each half separately. Evidence: bug-692, `.wolf/qa/fleet-section-coverage-verifier.md` control E.
- [2026-08-18] An empty filter result is not a finding until you prove the input was non-empty. Checking "how many registry paths lie outside the main root" with `x.path || x.dir` extracted ZERO paths (entries use `root`), so `0 outside` meant `0 examined` — and it was reported as a substantive correction to a reviewer who was actually right (2 of 85 are outside: `/mnt/s/MT5 Exness 1`, `/mnt/j/projecthomepaul/...`). Same vacuous-zero class as the `grep -L` bug it was written to replace. Any count-based check must assert its denominator: extracted == entries, else fail closed. Evidence: bug-691, `scripts/verify-fleet-section.mjs` schema-drift guard.
- [2026-08-18] Fleet-coverage checks must iterate `~/.openwolf/registry.json`, never a `**` path glob. `shopt globstar` is OFF in the hook/session shell, so `/mnt/j/projectshome/**/.wolf/OPENWOLF.md` matched 1 file where the registry holds 85; and `grep -L` on a non-matching glob prints nothing and exits 2 — byte-identical to full coverage. Any coverage verifier must assert `checked == registry.length` and fail closed on zero-examined, or a propagation failure reads as success. Evidence: `.wolf/qa/fleet-section-coverage-verifier.md`, `scripts/verify-fleet-section.mjs`.
- [2026-08-18] A "test that turns red when the real answer lands" is a change-detector, not proof a placeholder is load-bearing: `assert SEAM == <placeholder>` stays green after every call site is deleted. Pin placeholders with a BEHAVIOURAL assertion that fails when the seam is disconnected from its consumers, and record the negative control. Applied when adopting the `## Parked Questions` protocol section.
- [2026-08-12] A syntax-only diff is not defect evidence: string/token substitutions, boolean-operator changes, and large structural rewrites must not auto-file durable bugs. Keep auto-detection to narrow defensible categories, name the actual edited basename, and leave inferred records `status: open` until proof exists. Similarity matching must not let a short generic message absorb a longer distinct defect. Concurrency proof must use real asynchronous processes with deliberately dissimilar messages so coalescing cannot make lost writes look correct. Evidence: `.wolf/qa/auto-bug-detector-precision.md`.
- [2026-08-12] Cross-project quality feedback must disclose the exact ownership decision it acted on. Put the canonical owner root and absolute QA directory inspected before truncatable detail; preserve nearest-owner resolution and suppress unattributed files rather than falling back to the driving project. Evidence: `.wolf/qa/conclusion-owner-path-diagnostics.md`.

- [2026-08-12] Transcript records labeled as user turns can contain Claude Code harness envelopes, command output, agent messages, and continuation summaries. Before intent classification, structurally remove complete known wrappers, preserve adjacent attributable user text, and fail closed on malformed or truncated wrappers; never treat the raw turn as automatically user-authored evidence. Evidence: `.wolf/qa/learning-rule-boilerplate-filter.md`.
- [2026-08-08] Secret-token regexes must encode each prefix's actual separator; do not group `sk-`, `ghp_`, `github_pat_`, and `xox*-` behind one shared hyphen. The Mem0 canary initially accepted a synthetic `ghp_...` token as an `always` correction until the prefix alternatives were made explicit. Keep a safety-critical negative fixture and deliberate weakened-treatment falsifier. Evidence: `.wolf/qa/mem0-canary-2026-08-08.md` (bug-621).
- [2026-08-08] A hash-bound AI evaluation report proves only that the report is internally consistent; it does not prove a fresh agent executed the protected prompt, that treatment/control used comparable executor/model/effort/context, that cohort labels represent independent replication, or that self-reported events/costs occurred. Do not promote behavioral instructions from plain report artifacts. Require trustworthy execution provenance and measured telemetry, or fail closed as inconclusive. The Superpowers canary was exhausted rather than adding signing/provider infrastructure. Evidence: `.wolf/qa/superpowers-canary-scorer.md`.
- [2026-08-08] Durable ledger writers must lock, reread under the lock, allocate from the maximum numeric suffix, and commit with the strict fsynced atomic writer. Never allocate from array length, never resolve a duplicate ID with first-match `find()`, and never bulk read-modify-write hook-shared ledgers without the canonical lock. Historical collisions must preserve every record and leave ambiguous references unchanged; use `wolfpack ledger audit` then explicit `ledger repair --apply` with backup/receipt proof.
- [2026-08-08] Recoverable malformed ledgers must be normalized, not deleted: wrap legacy arrays into canonical object roots, retain invalid IDs as record-local provenance, allocate replacements above the maximum suffix, keep references unchanged, and require exact-byte backup/receipt proof. Recovery paths must bind canonical real project/ledger/backup paths while still accepting legitimate symlink spellings of the same project. Evidence: `.wolf/qa/ledger-normalization-recovery.md`.

- [2026-08-06] When verifying another project from a driving session, use `npm --prefix <project> ...` or an explicit `cd`; Bash starts in the driving project and a bare `npm run ...` can fail against the wrong directory. (bug-521)
- [2026-06-13] Do not instruct assistants to manually mark reviewlog entries completed; use `node .wolf/hooks/complete-review.js review-NNNN --reviewer <name> --summary "<outcome>"` so hashes are refreshed and review nudges coalesce.
- [2026-06-13] Never use synchronous busy-wait loops in OpenWolf hooks/runtime code. Daemon start/init paths must be idempotent against PM2 state, and port allocation must test the same wildcard bind mode the daemon uses.
- [2026-06-16] After editing TypeScript hook sources, verify and synchronize compiled/runtime JS copies before claiming hook behavior changed.
- [2026-06-17] Review completion supersede must be based on each pending file's current hash being covered by completed reviews, not file-set subset/superset containment.
- [2026-06-17] Quality-gate reductions belong to the edited file's nearest `.wolf/qa` in cross-project sessions, and language-specific test files should not become source reduction obligations.
- [2026-06-17] When a falsifier crosses a process, shell, network, file, or tool boundary, test the receiving context rather than grepping producer source; presence is not correctness.
- [2026-06-19] To verify another project has the latest fork, check both the global `openwolf` symlink target and the project `.wolf/hooks/stop.js` / `complete-review.js` markers.
- [2026-06-20] Never sync self-hosted `.wolf/cerebrum.md` or `.wolf/anatomy.md` into `src/templates/` or `templates/wolf/`; templates must stay generic.
- [2026-06-21] Stop-hook nudges should use Claude Code's JSON stdout contract with `decision: "block"` and exit 0; do not use stderr + exit 2 for normal Wolfpack feedback.
- [2026-07-06] Prefer reviewer-saw-this-hash receipts over manual assertions. `complete-review.js --reviewed-hash <manifest>` and `wolfpack review hash/complete` are the safe path; keep `--reviewed-current` only as fallback.
- [2026-07-14] Falsifiers for path-scoped gates must run outside excluded scratch paths such as `/tmp/**`; otherwise a missing nudge may prove only that the exclusion worked, not that the gate failed.
- [2026-07-18] Path-scoped gate tests need a positive control too: a file outside every exclude pattern (including `.txt`, which has no dedicated exclusion) must still fire, or a "passing" exclusion test may be vacuous. Applied in the Windows scratchpad regression tests (fixture under `$HOME`, not `/tmp`).
- [2026-07-26] A recovery path must preserve DATA, not merely REPORT the problem. bug-471's first fix quarantined corrupt nudge state and reported it, but still let the empty fallback overwrite the real file — the wrong invariant was asserted ("corruption is reported") instead of the load-bearing one ("the dispositions still exist"). When a fix handles a failure, write the falsifier against the data that must survive. Fixed via the `UNSAFE_TO_PERSIST` symbol, which makes `writeStateOrThrow` refuse to persist a fallback whose quarantine failed.
- [2026-07-26] Mutual exclusion is not proven by timing. Contenders acquiring at intervals matching the hold time only *implies* serialization. Prove it directly: inside the critical section, create a witness file with `{ flag: "wx" }` — a second simultaneous holder collides and the test reports overlap. Used to arbitrate the bug-477 lock-reclaim fix across 8 concurrent processes.
- [2026-07-26] When a monkeypatched/negative-control copy of an ESM module is written to `/tmp`, its sibling relative imports fail with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND and the control comes back inconclusive — which reads like a pass. Write the patched probe *alongside* the real module (e.g. `dist/src/hooks/nudges/__naive_probe.js`) and delete it after.
- [2026-07-26] An external reviewer's severity is a hypothesis, not a verdict. GPT-5.5 reported a CRITICAL "silent failure" whose falsifier was unrunnable (deleted stage dir, invented a `hashFile` export where the real one is `hashAll`); a with/without control showed identical output, so the silence came from the size threshold, not a bug — actual severity MEDIUM. Verify empirically before acting, and check that a CLEAN verdict echoes the reviewed scope hash so it is bound to the bytes actually reviewed.
- [2026-07-14] Regexes that target literal `.` or `:/` pathspecs must not end with `\b`; use a separator lookahead such as `(?=\s|$|;|&|\|)` or destructive Git forms like `git checkout -- .` silently miss.
- [2026-07-18] Git-init nudge for non-git repos must bypass the materiality gate (min_written_files, min_changed_lines, material_paths) because scope_excludes like `/tmp/**` can filter all writes and make `material=false` even when legitimate work was done. Use `hasAnyWrites` (unfiltered) to decide.
- [2026-07-18] Simplicity nudge added: fires at 500+ output tokens, max 1/session, reminding assistant to check YAGNI, readability, and efficiency. Configurable via `openwolf.simplicity`. [UPDATED 2026-07-19: default threshold raised to 2500 tokens — 500 fired on every substantive session and became noise — and the nudge is suppressed on stops where the review or quality gate already fired (advisory yields to actionable).]
- [2026-07-19] Stop-hook nudges are terse one/two-liners by default (user direction: "AI is smart and very simple and concise messages will work fine"). Do not re-expand nudge text with multi-question bullet lists or repeated rationale; `hook_messages.verbosity: "verbose"` keeps full guidance for onboarding. Reduction: .wolf/qa/terse-nudge-consolidation.md
- [2026-07-18] `tryConsumeNudgeSlot(capN=0)` must mean "unlimited" (no cap), not "zero allowed". The `??` operator already distinguishes `0` from `undefined`, but the slot consumer itself must short-circuit `capN === 0` before `prior >= capN` to avoid blocking all nudges when a user explicitly sets `max_fires_per_session: 0`.
- [2026-07-18] PM2 daemon ownership must require all three signals: an `openwolf-` process name, the `wolf-daemon.js` executable, and a matching absolute project root/cwd. An environment variable alone is not safe deletion proof.
- [2026-07-18] Keep Wolfpack PM2 daemons and the dashboard disabled by default. Explicit dashboard startup must use managed PM2 lifecycle and HTTP health identity, never an unmanaged detached child or a bare TCP-port readiness check.
- [2026-07-18] Project identity plus healthy status does not prove dashboard readiness: a background-only daemon exposes health while intentionally omitting UI routes. Health/readiness must also report and require `dashboard_enabled: true` before `openwolf dashboard` takes its reuse fast path.
- [2026-07-19] Absence of evidence in the channels you checked is not evidence of absence. The original bug-434 forensics enumerated only `type:"user"` transcript entries and concluded mid-turn messages were silently discarded; the client actually delivers them as `{type:"attachment", attachment:{type:"queued_command"}}` entries. Before concluding loss, enumerate ALL entry types the channel can emit. (bug-434, reduction: .wolf/qa/queue-drop-watchdog.md)
- [2026-07-21] Hooks must never treat "tool not found" as "check failed": bare `execFileSync("git", ...)` PATH lookups fail on Windows when Claude Code inherits a stale-shell PATH, and ENOENT conflated with rev-parse failure made the git gate advise `git init` on real repos (bug-437). Resolve binaries robustly (env/config override → PATH → well-known install locations) and keep tool-missing, check-failed, and check-passed as distinct states with distinct advice.
- [2026-07-22] Session-cumulative estimates must not drive per-event triggers: any counter that only grows (output tokens, lines, reads) will eventually attribute ALL prior work to the next small event (bug-441: 1-line comment edit reported "~76 lines changed"). Record a baseline (covered_tokens) on the artifact that consumes the work and trigger on the delta. When the baseline lives on shared state (reviewlog entries), updates must be session-scoped — a cross-session write poisons the other session's baseline and permanently suppresses its trigger.
- [2026-07-22] Nudge text should use project-relative paths; absolute paths were ~30% of the review nudge's bytes. Companion/complete-review resolve relative paths from invocation cwd and fail loudly on a wrong cwd, so brevity costs no safety.
- [2026-07-23] When defining a rubric/scale/vocabulary in protocol docs, align with the actual downstream contract, not the source text that inspired it: the severity rubric copied the external feedback's 3-tier HIGH-top scale while the companion runtime emits `LOW | MEDIUM | HIGH | CRITICAL` (companion-runtime.mjs), so identical defects got different labels across documents (bug-448). Also: when telling a reviewer a fix "now reads X", verify the edit actually landed — the first rubric fix edited item 3 only while the verification request claimed item 1 was fixed, and GLM correctly caught the residual.
- [2026-07-26] A hook rule that combines SESSION-WIDE activity (`session.files_written`) with a PROJECT-LOCAL `.wolf/` file must resolve ownership per file, or it misattributes across projects (bug-462: six writes in project B produced a 45.8h-stale warning about driving-project A, whose cerebrum was irrelevant, while B's was fresh). Use `groupByOwner()` / `resolveOwningProject()`. On ambiguous ownership, SUPPRESS low-severity nudges and log the ambiguity — never fall back to the driving project. Audit every rule using `files_written`/`files_read` for this class.
- [2026-07-26] Dedup that is not evidence-based cannot converge (bug-463): session COUNTERS permit N repeats of identical state, and hashing the assistant's rendered TEXT re-arms whenever the model rephrases the same recap. Fingerprint the DECISION EVIDENCE (all relevant files + their content hashes + schema version), never the message. Corollary: never fingerprint only the first N *displayed* files — a 6th changed file behind a "+N more" truncation would look unchanged.
- [2026-07-26] A cap keyed on content hash is not a cap: every fix mints a new hash, resetting the counter, which is how a documented 3-round review protocol ran 7 rounds. Bind the cap to a LINEAGE id derived from the file set (stable across content changes), then escalate once and go quiet.
- [2026-07-26] A fault-injection test MUST assert the injection actually executed. Monkeypatching `fs.writeFileSync` from a test file cannot intercept an ESM live binding inside the module under test — tests 18/19 went green while `injected === 0`, measuring nothing. Fixed with an injectable `io` seam in state.ts + an `assert(injected > 0)` precondition. Same applies to concurrency: `spawnSync` serializes children and cannot exercise a TOCTOU window; use `spawn` with staggered starts.
- [2026-07-23] Buglog IDs are NOT unique-enforced (bug-440 exists twice: an old resolved async-fix entry and the open registry-crash entry). When updating a buglog entry programmatically, filter on `id` AND `status` and assert exactly one match before writing — a plain `find(b => b.id === ...)` can silently update the wrong entry.
- [2026-08-07] A `node -e`/script read-modify-write on `.wolf/buglog.json` races a concurrently-firing Wolfpack hook that ALSO appends entries. At commit b10ad01 this dropped 245→201 entries (44 lost) and minted a duplicate, because the hook's append landed between my read and my write and my write clobbered it. The buglog is NOT a safe read-modify-write target while hooks are live. Mitigations: snapshot a count before AND after the write and assert equality; if the count drops, restore from `git show HEAD:.wolf/buglog.json` and re-apply only the intended delta; or stop the hook subsystem before bulk edits. Prefer `complete-review.js`-style atomic helpers over hand-rolled JSON edits on hook-shared files. (bug-534/535 session; restored in 0df2ea9)
- [2026-08-12] Acquiring the canonical buglog lock does not make a stale pre-lock snapshot safe: the learning-filter bug writer read a previously truncated 320-record live ledger under the lock and preserved that loss. Always compare the live ledger against the committed/base corpus before mutation; recovery must merge verified additions onto the complete baseline, then atomically write under the canonical lock. This session restored 359 baseline records plus 7 additions (366 total).

- [2026-07-27] Registering `process.on("uncaughtException")` or `"unhandledRejection"` is NOT passive observation — it REPLACES Node's default disposition. Without a listener an uncaught throw prints a stack and exits 1; with a bare listener the process logs and KEEPS RUNNING, exiting 0 (measured both ways). I shipped this into the Stop hook as "diagnostics" and it silently broke the hook's failure semantics — Claude Code parses hook stdout as a JSON contract, so continuing in a corrupted state can emit output accepted as valid. Always restore the default with `process.exit(1)` inside the handler. Instrument by RECORDING, never by INTERCEPTING. See bug-483 and `.wolf/qa/hook-lifecycle-instrumentation.md`.
- [2026-07-27] `openwolf update` with no arguments is FLEET-WIDE, not cwd-scoped: it iterates every project in `~/.openwolf/registry.json` and ignores the directory you run it from. A sandbox copy under /tmp is therefore NOT exercised by it, and running it "just to test" writes to every registered project. Registry entries key the project path as `root` (not `path`/`dir`) — guessing that field silently reports every project missing.
- [2026-07-27] A shipped `stop.js` legitimately differs from `templates/wolf/hooks/stop.js` by exactly the `//# sourceMappingURL=` footer. Do not treat that hash mismatch as staleness; diff with the footer stripped before concluding a project is out of date.
- [2026-07-27] Reduction `target-hash` values go stale the moment a follow-up commit touches the documented file. Re-verify every `target-hash*` in a reduction against `sha256sum` before claiming the reduction is current — a reduction marked current for bytes that no longer exist is worse than none. (Caught two: stop.ts and update.ts.)
- [2026-07-27] `node --test tests/` is not a directory walk on Node 22 — it resolves `tests` as a MODULE and fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND, reporting a bogus `# fail 1`. Use `npm test` or `node --test 'tests/**/*.test.js'`. Do not diagnose a suite failure before confirming the invocation is well-formed.
- [2026-07-27] Nudge gates must key on the OBLIGATION, not on the edit. "Edited 3+ times" only implies a bug fix for artifacts whose correctness is executable-checkable; three edits to prose is authoring. Before adding any nudge, ask what property makes the obligation real and gate on that — path globs and edit counts are proxies that drift. (bug-496..499, `.wolf/qa/nudge-obligation-scoping.md`)
- [2026-07-27] Do NOT make project adaptation frequency-based. "Scan the repo and treat common extensions as code" fails on this very repo: `.md` is the 3rd most common extension (70 js, 60 ts, 47 md), so prose would be classified as code — reintroducing the bug it was meant to fix, silently. Correct shape: a curated candidate registry INTERSECTED with what the project contains. Commonness never votes.
- [2026-07-27] For advisory gates, resolve every uncertain branch toward FIRING. A false positive is visible and ackable; a silently-disabled gate costs a real missed obligation and nobody finds out. Applied in `detectObligationExtensions` (empty/non-git repo -> full registry) and in the `covered_tokens_basis` unit check (ignore an unmarked baseline rather than subtract mismatched units and clamp to 0).
- [2026-07-27] `isCodeFile()` is NOT a general "is this code" predicate — it also excludes everything under `.wolf/`, which is right for the quality gate (reductions describe code, they aren't code) but wrong for the buglog nudge, where it would blind the gate on Wolfpack's own hooks. Check what a helper excludes before reusing it; the name undersells the behavior.
- [2026-07-27] When one concept has several implementations, fixing one site leaves the others firing. `post-write.ts` had a duplicate multi-edit nudge with NO excludes and NO cap that the external report never found. Grep for other emitters of the same message before declaring a nudge fixed, and put the shared predicate in `shared.js` (as `carriesBugfixObligation`/`globToRegex` now are).
- [2026-07-27] A pre-existing test can encode the defect as a requirement. `review-completion.test.js:1035` asserted the buglog nudge RE-FIRES after an acknowledgement — which was bug-497 written down as intended behavior. When a test fails after a deliberate semantic fix, read what it asserts before "fixing" the code back; update it with a negative control instead.
- [2026-07-27] An external reviewer's severity AND its stated mechanism are both hypotheses. The 2026-07-27 nudge report was right on two claims, but its third ("review nudge counts prose lines") was mechanically wrong — `effectiveLines` is `(sessionTokens - covered)/17`, a token-attribution bug, not a line-count bug, with a different fix. It also missed a fourth defect entirely. Verify by executing the code; the report's own caveat flagged that claim as inferred rather than isolated.
- [2026-07-27] **A test that reimplements the rule it tests can only confirm its author.** The attribution unit test defined its own `decide()` helper using `w.tokens` — the same wrong field name the implementation used — so 103 tests passed while the feature never executed once in production (bug-516/517). Falsify against the REAL producer's output, not against a restatement of the rule. When a test and the code share an assumption, the test proves nothing about that assumption. Concretely: drive fixtures through the same mapper/constructor the production path uses, and for cross-module contracts add a structural test that reads the shipped source and asserts producer and consumer agree on the field name.
- [2026-07-27] **Verify that a new regression test actually FAILS on the defect** before trusting it. Reintroduce the bug, watch the test go red for the intended reason, then restore. A test that passes on both broken and fixed code is worse than no test, because it manufactures confidence. Done for the producer/consumer field test (bug-517).
- [2026-07-27] When a value and the metadata describing it are written as two separate statements, they WILL disagree. `covered_tokens` was assigned unconditionally while `covered_tokens_basis` was stamped only under a condition, so a session-total value could carry a scoped label in two independent directions (bug-518). Write value+marker as one indivisible operation, and never `Math.max` across bases — comparing incommensurable scales is meaningless, so the current value must win outright.
- [2026-07-27] A safety rule that is unreachable is not a safety rule. bug-498's unit-safety refusal had never executed because the feature guarding it was inert; fixing the field name made it fire and broke two end-to-end tests (bug-520). When enabling previously-dead code, expect dormant branches to wake up — and check whether the newly-failing test encodes the OLD reachable behavior rather than the intended contract.
- [2026-07-27] When one predicate is shared by callers holding different data FORMS (absolute vs relative paths), anchored patterns silently mean different things at each call site — the same file got opposite answers from two hooks (bug-519). A shared predicate must either normalize its input or accept every form the callers hold; "one function" does not by itself buy "one semantics".
- [2026-07-27] Convergent findings from independent reviewers deserve a higher prior than either alone. ChatGPT and Kimi, given different prompts, independently reported the same field-name defect — that agreement was the strongest signal in a four-round ledger, and it was correct. Weight convergence, but still verify by execution before acting.

- [2026-08-08] For fleet releases, deploy to and verify a canary first, then update all registered projects without profile overrides, and follow deployment with a read-only health audit for malformed files, excessive corpus sizes, duplicate IDs, and other normally unseen state problems.
- [2026-08-08] Ledger repair must validate under the same file lock immediately before mutation, preserve first occurrence and array order, verify non-ID record digests after the atomic write, and inventory collided-ID references without rewriting ambiguous history. Reduction: `.wolf/qa/ledger-integrity-core.md`.

- **2026-08-19 — A process rule must name the command that satisfies it.** The Staged Rollout
  section mandated canary-first deployment but named no flag; `openwolf update` is
  fleet-wide by default and cwd does NOT scope it (`src/cli/update.ts:102`). Following the
  rule literally still wrote 84 projects. Canary with `openwolf update --project <name>`.
  When writing a governance rule, name the exact invocation — an unexecutable rule produces
  false confidence that staging happened. See bug-706, `.wolf/qa/canary-rollout-scope.md`.
- **2026-08-19 — Do not measure a fleet while a fleet write is in flight.** An interim
  `verify-fleet-section` run reported 5 MISSING; those files were mid-write and converged
  to the template moments later. Re-measure after the writer exits, and check process state
  before treating a partial reading as a finding.
- **2026-08-19 — A canary's success is invisible in a fleet-wide check.** Mid-canary the correct
  signature is 1 PASS and N DRIFTED. Without a single-project scope (`--only`), the
  canary's own correctness cannot be asserted and the expected FAIL reads as breakage.

- **2026-08-19 — `pgrep -f <pattern>` matches your own waiter shells.** A background
  `until ! pgrep -f "X"; do sleep; done` contains "X" in its own command string, so it
  waits on itself forever and reports the target as running after it exited. Match on the
  binary form (`pgrep -f '^node .*X'`) or check the count of real processes. This is the
  same self-match that killed a shell earlier via `pkill -f`.

- **2026-08-19 — Do not write a `reduction:` path from memory.** Two buglog entries cited
  QA files that did not exist (`driftcheck.md`, `experiment-journal.md`); the real ones were
  `drift-check-command.md` and, for bug-703, nothing at all — the proof had never been
  written. A dangling reduction link is a fix with no evidence, which is exactly what the
  field exists to prevent. Verify with `fs.existsSync` when writing the entry.
- **2026-08-19 — Extract paths before checking existence.** A first sweep flagged 8
  "dangling" links that were compound strings (path + prose, or two paths). Checking
  `startsWith('.wolf/') && existsSync(whole_string)` both mis-flags those and under-counts
  the denominator (127 vs the real 130). Regex out the `.md` paths, then check each.

- **2026-08-19 — Challenge companion findings before they drive edits.** A GLM review
  returned 5 findings; challenging them killed 2 outright. One claimed `writeJSON` does
  "a direct fs.writeFileSync" causing torn reads — it actually does tmp-write + renameSync
  (atomic on POSIX); the reviewer quoted code that does not exist. Another called the 0.8
  similarity threshold unreachable — measured 1.50 for identical and 1.33 for
  same-message-different-line, both merging. Read the cited source fresh; never trust the
  snippet in the report. Evidence: `.wolf/qa/post-write-dedup-path.md`.
- **2026-08-19 — When code contradicts its own comment, the comment is usually the spec.**
  `autoDetectBugFix` said "same file + same category" and compared `path.basename`, with
  the correct `relFile` computed 7 lines above and unused — the signature of a refactor
  slip. Both challenge rounds converged on REAL DEFECT from that single tell (bug-707).
- **2026-08-19 — A test with early-return guards can pass vacuously.** The dedup regression
  test returns early if auto-detection never fires, so "2 passing" was compatible with
  "nothing exercised". Probed the real hook to confirm entries were actually created before
  trusting the green.


## Decision Log

- [2026-08-19] Standardized a rapid-assessment coverage axis for adversarial panel reports: a 10-question yes/no checklist plus an X/10 summary row, alongside the existing narrative findings. Rationale: narrative-only reports make absence of coverage invisible — an axis nobody examined reads identically to an axis examined and found clean. A fixed question set forces every axis to be answered explicitly, and the X/10 figure makes partial coverage legible at a glance. Adopted as a report-format convention for panel-style reviews; it does not replace per-finding evidence, which remains the deliverable.

- 2026-06-09: Use canonical config `openwolf.claim_calibration` and log type `claim_calibration`; keep legacy `openwolf.scientific_mode` config and `scientific_mode` log suppression compatibility during migration.
- 2026-07-18: Simplicity nudge uses output-token threshold (not line count) because tokens are already tracked in session ledger; no new instrumentation needed. Default 500 tokens ≈ ~30 lines of code.
- 2026-07-19: Terse nudge consolidation (bug-436): multi-nudge stops injected ~800 tokens/turn of repeated boilerplate, contributing to the "AI too busy to read user input" latency the user observed. Simplicity default raised 500→2500 and advisory nudges yield to actionable gates. Measured 35% byte cut (2237→1463 chars) on a 4-eligible-nudge stop.
- 2026-07-21: External harness-coder feedback triage: implemented 5 of 10 items (--check dry-run, simplicity most-edited lens, buglog status field, nested .wolf/.gitignore + tracked buglog, reproduction_command in QA template). Rejected: gates_enforced assert-injection (their probe harness, not Wolfpack), per-claim-time reductions (covered by verify_conclusions sub-gate), companion retry (tony-local plugin-owned), anatomy auto-update (already in post-write.ts). Reduction: .wolf/qa/feedback-harness-improvements.md
- 2026-07-22: Grok nudge-verbosity feedback triage: implemented 2 items (bug-441 session-baseline delta for the review size trigger — cumulative token estimate made 1-line edits report "~76 lines changed"; project-relative paths in the review nudge, measured 986→768 chars). Already done before the feedback: terse one-line format + verbosity toggle (custom.10), capped repeats via (id, hash-tuple) nudge caps, "+N more" file lists. Rejected: comment-only auto-refresh (fragile classification, weakens review binding), single-summary batching (refactor cost > gain), probe-aware suppression (hooks can't see the harness task list), conciseness meta-gate. Reduction: .wolf/qa/review-baseline-delta.md
- 2026-07-23: External multi-round review-loop feedback triage: adopted 6 of 7 items as PROTOCOL (new "Multi-Round Review Convergence" subsection in OPENWOLF.md + one bullet in global CLAUDE.md review contract): root-cause ledger with NEW/EXISTING-incomplete tagging, delta-aware round-2+ prompts, severity rubric (HIGH = distinct reachable money/data/correctness path; no speculative future-extensibility), state-transition matrix requirement for stateful diffs, formal convergence rule (refresh → one clean current-byte review from a DIFFERENT provider → tests → --reviewed-current → stop), reviewer diversity at final arbitration. Item 2 (verified-invariant ledger) adopted only in its cheap half: invariants carried in the QA reduction and quoted in re-review prompts. REJECTED all automatic machinery: root-cause auto-clustering (semantic — that IS the reviewer's job; hooks are dumb JSON processors) and line-range invariant auto-invalidation (complex, and a stale "verified" invariant on a money path is worse than a re-check). No code changes — the review prompt contract is model-authored, so protocol docs are the correct layer.
- 2026-07-26: A "read-check-write under a lock" is NOT automatically safe — it only enforces the conditions it actually re-checks inside the lock. The nudge engine's per-rule session ceiling (bug-472) was filtered on a snapshot taken BEFORE the lock; `tryClaim` held the lock but never re-checked that count, so 8 concurrent processes with distinct fingerprints of the same rule all claimed (negative control: 8 emissions vs 1). When adding any new cross-process constraint, ask "is this predicate re-evaluated inside the critical section?" — and count in-flight leases, not just committed records, or the claim→commit window leaks.
- 2026-07-26: Never conflate "file absent" with "file unparseable" in state loaders. `readState` returned `emptyState()` for both, so a truncated `nudge-state.json` made the next write permanently erase every user dismissal (bug-471). Absent → empty is correct; corrupt → quarantine the bytes and surface a diagnostic. Also: an in-code comment asserting where an error "is reported" is not evidence — that comment named `writeStateOrThrow`, which only validates the body it is about to write, never the bytes just read. Verify the claim, don't trust the comment.
- 2026-07-26: Fingerprint/digest inputs must be canonicalized UNIFORMLY. `target_hashes` keys and `owner_root` were canonicalized while `evidence` was hashed raw, so two spellings of one path yielded two fingerprints and a dismissal bound to one failed to suppress the other (bug-471 sibling, finding 3). Canonicalize conservatively though: only absolute/UNC/drive paths, never relative fragments or prose, or the digest becomes dependent on `process.cwd()` at invocation time. Type-tag scalar values too — `String(h)` collapses `12345678` and `"12345678"`.
- 2026-07-26: In `src/hooks/nudges/`, `state.js`/`engine.js`/`project-scope.js` ARE byte-identical twins of their `.ts` files, but the files under `rules/` are NOT (pre-existing comment/whitespace drift). A blanket `cp *.ts *.js` sync is wrong for the rules directory — apply changes surgically there and grep the constant across all three layers (`src/`, `.wolf/`, `templates/wolf/`) to confirm it landed. A `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump that reaches only `.ts` is invisible at runtime.
- 2026-07-26: Repeated identical operational failures are a DEFECT SIGNAL, not friction to work around. I cleared a stale `.wolf/reviewlog.json.lock` by hand four times before investigating; the root cause (bug-477) was a 20-line ordering bug — `isLockReclaimable` checked owner liveness only AFTER `age > staleMs` (30s) while `acquireFileLock` times out at 2s, so a crashed hook's lock was unreclaimable for 30s. Freshness by mtime is NOT evidence a lock is still held. Fix: check the recorded pid's liveness before the mtime gate, behind a 250ms grace. Measured 2001ms hard failure → 2ms reclaim, with a live-owner control proving locks are still not stolen.
- 2026-07-26: `src/utils/size-discipline.js` is COMPILED OUTPUT (no `@ts-nocheck` header, trailing `//# sourceMappingURL=` footer), NOT a byte-identical twin of its `.ts` — unlike `src/hooks/nudges/{state,engine,project-scope}`. Copying `.ts` over it clobbers both markers. There are FOUR on-disk copies (`src/utils/*.ts`, `src/utils/*.js`, `.wolf/utils/*.js` which carries a `@ts-nocheck` header, `templates/wolf/utils/*.js` which matches `src/.js`). The runtime imports `.wolf/utils/`, so a src-only fix changes nothing at runtime — always `find . -name "<file>" -not -path "./node_modules/*"` and check each copy for the change marker.
- 2026-07-26: Auto-detected buglog stubs (generic `error_message` like "Type error" / "Missing error handling in X", no `status`, no `root_cause`, no `reduction`) get written by a hook while files are mid-edit, and they SQUAT the next free bug ID — an idempotency check on `id` alone will then silently skip writing the real entry. Verify each stub before deleting (bug-476 claimed missing error handling in `readLockPid`; it already had a try/catch, confirmed by probing "notanumber"/""/"-5"/"0"), then filter on `!x.status && !x.reduction` and re-check per-ID counts.
- 2026-07-26: When a RECOVERY path can itself fail, verify the fallback preserves DATA, not merely that it REPORTS honestly. bug-474 was an incomplete fix for bug-471: the failed-quarantine branch fired `onCorrupt` with `quarantine:null` (honest) but returned an ordinary empty state, so the next write destroyed the only surviving copy anyway. I had probed that exact branch and asserted "corruption still reported" — the wrong invariant. Ask "does the user's data still exist afterwards?", not "did we log it correctly?"
- 2026-07-26: Do not write JSON entries to `.wolf/buglog.json` via `node -e` inside a bash heredoc — apostrophes in prose terminate the shell quote and can commit a TRUNCATED entry before the syntax error surfaces (this produced a bogus `"Type error"` bug-473 alongside the real one). Write the script to the scratchpad with the Write tool and run it as a file; make it idempotent by checking `bugs.some(x => x.id === id)` first, and re-verify per-ID counts after appending.
- 2026-07-26: An external reviewer's SEVERITY is a hypothesis, not a verdict — verify reachability with a control before acting on it. A companion reported CRITICAL "false silence" for the review-snapshot bug (bug-473); running the gate with and without the stale pending review produced IDENTICAL output, proving the silence came from the size threshold working as designed. The defect was real but MEDIUM (attestation integrity: a stale entry could later be completed as covering bytes its reviewer never received). Also: reviewers guess export names — the supplied falsifier called a non-existent `hashFile` (real export: `hashAll`) and referenced its own deleted stage dir, so rebuild falsifiers against the actual module.
- 2026-07-26: Changing a fingerprint algorithm silently invalidates every stored disposition. Bump the participating `SCHEMA_VERSION` in the same commit so the invalidation is explicit and auditable rather than presenting as a mysterious mass re-arm of previously-dismissed nudges.
- 2026-07-23: Writer "Harness Effect" article triage (vendor self-reported preprint, arXiv:2607.06906 — numbers directional, not audited): most levers already embodied (guardrails-in-code = hooks; anti-tokenmaxxing = terse nudges w/ measured byte cuts; two-zone prompt = companion runtime structure + Claude Code prefix caching; routing = budget profile). Adopted ONE gap: review-loop round cap (failure-spend governance) as item 6 of Multi-Round Review Convergence — 3 rounds still producing new verified findings → escalate to user instead of looping. Banked as corroboration: their delegation cliff (small models 0.42-0.45 orchestration reliability vs 0.85+ frontier) externally validates the budget profile (budget companions get bounded single-purpose reviews, strong models get arbitration); their "harness leverage" rule (feature must remove more task tokens than it adds in coordination tokens) = Wolfpack's measured-nudge-byte test. Rejected: CPM instrumentation (heavy at this scale; token-ledger suffices), learned ACRouter-style routing (out of scope). Template-only until next fleet deploy.
